title: Two sum
summary: Return the indices of the two numbers in `nums` that add up to `target`, smaller index first.
hints: Pick any number in the array. What exact value would its partner need to have?
Checking every pair works but repeats a lot of looking. As you move through the array, remember the numbers you have already passed, so that "have I seen the partner?" takes one step.
Keep a map from value to index. For each number, look up target minus that number in the map before adding the number itself.
pattern: Remember what you have seen (map lookup)
takeaway: One pass with a map from value to index is O(n). The nested-loop version is O(n^2) and fails the large test. Whenever you catch yourself searching the same data again and again, a map or set can usually answer in one step.

tests.label: large input: 200,000 numbers, the pair is at the very end
